**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 24, 2026
**Re:** Kunoux Creamery, Inc.: Review of Tilil Systems DairyLedger SaaS license documents (matter s64-m0002)

---

## 1. Summary

We act for Kunoux Creamery, Inc. (Kunoux). Kunoux is the Licensee under a Software-as-a-Service License Agreement with Tilil Systems, Inc. (Tilil) dated March 1, 2026. The agreement is governed by Delaware law and has a **five-year Initial Term** running to February 28, 2031 (License Agreement §14.1). The Annual Subscription Fee is **$486,000 per year**, or $2,430,000 over the Initial Term (Order Form §2). Kunoux's parent, **Kunoux Holdings, L.P., is the guarantor under the Parent Guaranty**. The guaranty covers all Licensee obligations, including indemnities and amounts accelerated under §14.4 (Parent Guaranty preamble, §1.1 and §2.1).

I reviewed all ten documents in the folder:

- License Agreement
- SOW No. 1
- Amendment No. 1
- Order Form No. 1
- Term Sheet
- Parent Guaranty
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA)
- Quality Agreement
- Press release
- Kickoff minutes

The press release and minutes raise no new issues. They do confirm the commercial understanding that the deal covered only the two Wisconsin plants.

I found four material issues, set out below in priority order. Issue 1 is time-critical because of the pending Ostrander transaction. The consent we need from Tilil also gives us the best leverage to fix Issues 2 to 4 in a single Amendment No. 2.

| Priority | Issue | Location | Exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (Urgent / High)** | Pending Ostrander sale triggers Tilil's change-of-control termination and fee acceleration | License Agreement §14.4 and §1 ("Change of Control"); Amendment No. 1 Recital B and §5.1 | Loss of platform on 30 days' notice, plus roughly $1.46M–$1.94M of accelerated fees, which are guaranteed by the parent |
| **2 (High)** | Kunoux's data indemnity is uncapped, while Tilil's DPA liability stays capped | DPA §8.1–8.3; License Agreement §12.2, §12.4, §16.4 | Unlimited liability for Kunoux and its parent for data claims, including claims caused by Tilil |
| **3 (High)** | Exclusivity reaches every current and future facility of Kunoux and its Affiliates worldwide | License Agreement §2.6; Order Form §3.1; compare Term Sheet §4.1 | Restricts group operations and M&A; post-closing it may reach Ostrander portfolio companies |
| **4 (Medium-High)** | Tilil can assign freely to a buyer of "any part" of its business, including a competitor | License Agreement §15.1; §1 ("Permitted Transferee") | Kunoux's supplier, pricing and quality data could pass to a rival; the guaranty follows the contract |

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Change of control from the Ostrander sale (URGENT / HIGH)

**Location:**
- License Agreement §14.4 and the §1 definition of "Change of Control"
- Amendment No. 1 Recital B and §5.1
- Parent Guaranty §1.1(b)

**What the documents say:**
- **The trigger.** Under §14.4, Tilil may terminate on **30 days' written notice** if Licensee "undergoes a Change of Control without Licensor's prior written consent."
- **The acceleration.** On such a termination, "all Subscription Fees for the remainder of the Initial Term shall become immediately due and payable."
- **The definition.** "Change of Control" includes any **direct or indirect** transfer of more than 50% of the voting equity of Licensee "or of any entity controlling Licensee."
- **The transaction.** Amendment No. 1 (dated October 2, 2026), Recital B, records that Kunoux Holdings, L.P. signed an equity purchase agreement on September 18, 2026. Under it, Holdings will sell the equity of its general partner and operating subsidiaries to **Ostrander Dairy Partners III, L.P.** Closing is expected in Q1 2027. That sale is an indirect Change of Control of Kunoux.
- **No consent in the Amendment.** Amendment §5.1 states that, except as expressly set out in Sections 2 and 3, "nothing herein constitutes a consent or waiver under the Agreement." Neither Section 2 nor Section 3 addresses change of control.
- **Tilil knows about the deal.** Amendment §2.1 expanded the confidentiality carve-out to allow disclosure to prospective acquirers. Tilil is therefore aware of the transaction but has reserved its rights. Nothing in the folder shows that consent has been requested or obtained.

**Why it matters:**
- **Loss of a critical system.** Tilil could cut off the platform that runs Kunoux's raw-milk receiving, lot genealogy and recall functions at Eau Claire, with only 30 days' notice. The termination would also come during the Sheboygan go-live window (M6 is now January 18, 2027).
- **Accelerated fees.** If closing occurs before March 1, 2027, Years 2–5 would be accelerated: about **$1,944,000**. If closing occurs after the Year 2 invoice is paid, Years 3–5 would be accelerated: about **$1,458,000**.
- **The parent pays too.** The accelerated amount is a Guaranteed Obligation under Parent Guaranty §1.1(b). Holdings' obligations are absolute and survive changes in ownership (§3.1(f)). Ostrander will see this as a contingent liability in diligence.
- **Leverage on renegotiation.** Tilil can use the threat of termination to extract price or other concessions.
- **Post-closing notice duty.** Separately, Kunoux must notify Tilil within 10 Business Days after closing (§14.4).

**Recommended fix:**
1. Before closing, obtain Tilil's **written consent to, and waiver of, §14.4 for the Ostrander transaction**. It should be signed under §16.11 and acknowledged by Holdings.
2. Ideally, also amend §14.4 so that:
   - a change of control of Kunoux to a non-competitor of Tilil does not need consent; or
   - in any case, termination does **not** accelerate fees, and Kunoux keeps its §14.6 transition rights.
3. Flag the issue now to the M&A team acting on the Ostrander sale. Tilil's consent should be a closing deliverable, or the purchase agreement should allocate this risk.
4. Use the consent request as the vehicle for an Amendment No. 2 that also fixes Issues 2–4.

---

### Issue 2: Uncapped Licensee data indemnity (HIGH)

**Location:**
- DPA §8.1, §8.2 and §8.3
- License Agreement §12.2, §12.4 and §16.4

**What the documents say:**
- **The indemnity.** DPA §8.1 requires Kunoux to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Tilil, its Affiliates and its **Subprocessors** against all losses, fines, penalties and costs "arising out of or relating to Licensee Data or Licensee's processing instructions." This expressly includes claims by Data Subjects and regulators.
- **No cap for Kunoux.** DPA §8.2 provides that this indemnity "shall not be subject to any limitation of liability in the Agreement, including Section 12."
- **Cap for Tilil.** DPA §8.3 keeps **Tilil's** DPA liability subject to Section 12. That cap is fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months, roughly $486,000 (§12.2).
- **The License Agreement defers to the DPA.** License Agreement §12.4 applies the cap "except as otherwise expressly provided in the DPA."
- **Precedence.** §16.4 gives the DPA precedence on personal data matters.
- **Conclusion.** The carve-out operates as drafted. Kunoux's DPA indemnity is **not** subject to the 12-month-fees cap.

**Why it matters:**
- **Breadth of the trigger.** "Licensee Data" is defined broadly in License Agreement §1. It covers farm supplier, driver (including GPS geolocation), pricing and consumer-complaint records, some with health information. "Arising out of or relating to" Licensee Data covers almost any data incident.
- **No fault requirement.** The indemnity has no carve-out for Tilil's own breach, negligence or security failure. A breach at Tilil or one of its subprocessors (for example, Northfield Cloud Services) could result in Kunoux indemnifying Tilil, without limit, for claims Tilil caused. Meanwhile, Kunoux's recovery against Tilil stays capped.
- **No offset from insurance.** Tilil's insurance (cyber cover of $5M under §16.7) does not reduce Kunoux's exposure.
- **The parent is exposed.** The indemnity is expressly guaranteed by Kunoux Holdings, L.P. (Parent Guaranty §1.1(d)). This also matters to Ostrander.
- **Departure from the deal.** The Term Sheet (§11.2–11.3) contemplated a mutual cap, with uncapped exclusions limited to fraud, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, the IP indemnities, fees and personal injury. A one-way data carve-out was never agreed.

**Recommended fix:** Amend DPA §8:
1. Delete §8.2, so the indemnity falls under §12.2. Alternatively, agree a **mutual, separately negotiated data super-cap** (for example, a multiple of annual fees) that applies equally to Tilil's data and security liabilities.
2. Narrow §8.1 to losses **to the extent caused by** Kunoux's breach of the DPA, its unlawful instructions or its failure to give required notices or obtain required consents (DPA §2.4).
3. Expressly exclude losses caused by Tilil's or its Subprocessors' breach, negligence or Security Incidents.
4. Add a reciprocal Tilil indemnity for Security Incidents and breaches of the DPA.

---

### Issue 3: Overbroad exclusivity (HIGH)

**Location:**
- License Agreement §2.6, read with the §1 definition of "Covered Facilities"
- Order Form §3.1
- Compare Term Sheet §4.1 and Annex A

**What the documents say:**
- **The covenant.** §2.6 bars Kunoux, and requires it to cause its Affiliates not to, "license, subscribe to or use" any third-party (or internally developed) software performing the Traceability Functions "at any Covered Facility."
- **The definition.** "Covered Facilities" is defined by reference to the Order Form. Order Form §3.1 defines it as "all facilities owned, leased or operated by Licensee or any of its Affiliates, **wherever located**." It expressly includes facilities acquired after March 1, 2026.
- **The combined effect.** Because §2.6 incorporates that definition, there is no conflict for §16.4 to resolve. The covenant applies worldwide, to every current and future plant, receiving station, warehouse, distribution center and lab of the Kunoux group.
- **What was agreed.** Term Sheet §4.1 limited exclusivity to "milk traceability software at the Eau Claire and Sheboygan, Wisconsin plants only." Term Sheet §3.5 excluded rollout to other facilities.
- **The rest of the deal reflects two plants.** The SOW (§2.8(a)), the Order Form hardware and entitlements, and the press release all reflect two plants.

**Why it matters:**
- **Current operations.** Kunoux cannot use any other traceability tool anywhere in the group for five years. That includes plants that are not on DairyLedger and are not licensed under the SOW.
- **The Ostrander effect.** After closing, Ostrander's other portfolio companies under common control may become "Affiliates" of Kunoux. Kunoux would then be obliged to cause them to comply, which would put it in breach if they use competing systems.
- **Acquisitions.** Any acquired facility immediately becomes subject to the covenant. This forces either a migration to DairyLedger or a breach.
- **Limited remedy from the Term Sheet.** The Term Sheet is non-binding (§14.1), so it supports a renegotiation argument but is unlikely to be a reliable basis for reformation.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend §2.6 so that, for exclusivity purposes, the covenant applies only to the **Eau Claire and Sheboygan plants** (or to facilities where the Subscription Services are actually in production use).
2. Expressly exclude:
   - Affiliates that are not subsidiaries of Kunoux Creamery, Inc.; and
   - facilities acquired after the Order Form Date, unless Kunoux elects to add them by a new Order Form.
3. Keep the broad Covered Facilities definition only for the license grant (§2.1).

---

### Issue 4: Unrestricted assignment by Tilil (MEDIUM-HIGH)

**Location:**
- License Agreement §15.1 and the §1 definition of "Permitted Transferee"
- Related: Parent Guaranty §7.1

**What the documents say:**
- **Apparent mutuality.** §15.1 appears mutual: neither party may assign without consent, except "to a Permitted Transferee upon written notice."
- **The one-sided definition.** "Permitted Transferee" means:
  - (a) any Affiliate of either party; or
  - (b) "any successor to all or **any part of Licensor's business or assets** to which this Agreement relates."
- **No protections.** Limb (b) has no Kunoux equivalent, no requirement that the acquirer buy all or substantially all of the business, no financial-capability test, no exclusion of competitors and no requirement of a written assumption.
- **The guaranty follows.** Under Parent Guaranty §7.1, the benefit of the guaranty passes to the assignee automatically.

**Why it matters:**
- **Data in a rival's hands.** Tilil could sell the DairyLedger line, or just a piece of it, to a rival dairy processor or its technology arm. The license, the hosted Licensee Data (supplier identities, milk pricing and premiums, quality results) and the right to enforce the parent guaranty would all pass without Kunoux's consent.
- **Kunoux would still be locked in.** Kunoux would remain bound by exclusivity (Issue 3) and the fee commitment.
- **Asymmetry.** Kunoux, by contrast, needs consent for any transfer outside its Affiliates.

**Recommended fix:** Limit limb (b) to a successor to **all or substantially all** of Tilil's business that:
- is not a Kunoux competitor (define the term, for example dairy processors, cooperatives and their affiliates);
- assumes the Agreement in writing; and
- has financial standing comparable to Tilil's.

In addition:
- Require advance notice to Kunoux.
- Give Kunoux a right to terminate without acceleration, with §14.6 transition assistance and release from §2.6, if the transferee is or becomes a competitor.
- Consider a reciprocal right for Kunoux to assign to a successor to its business. This is helpful given the Ostrander transaction.

---

## 3. Other observations (lower priority)

- **Acceleration on Licensor termination for cause (§14.5(d)).** This clause also accelerates all remaining fees. It is worth softening in the same amendment, for example to a mitigated damages measure.
- **Guaranty amendments without consent.** Parent Guaranty §1.2 and §3.1(a) bind Holdings to amendments made without its consent. Ostrander's counsel will likely want Holdings released, or a replacement guarantor arrangement, at closing.
- **No action needed on the remaining documents.** The Quality Agreement, SOW and Amendment No. 1 operational changes raise no material concerns. The kickoff minutes and press release are consistent with a two-plant deal.

## 4. Recommended next steps

1. **This week.** Brief the client and its M&A counsel on Issue 1. Confirm the target closing date and whether the equity purchase agreement addresses third-party consents.
2. **Approach Tilil promptly** for a §14.4 consent and waiver. Present it together with a proposed Amendment No. 2 that addresses:
   - the DPA §8 cap and fault standard (Issue 2);
   - exclusivity scope (Issue 3); and
   - the Permitted Transferee definition (Issue 4).
3. **Have Kunoux Holdings, L.P. acknowledge Amendment No. 2**, as it did Amendment No. 1.
4. **Calendar** the 10-Business-Day post-closing notice obligation under §14.4.

I am happy to prepare a draft consent letter and Amendment No. 2 on your instruction.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate, Technology Transactions
**Date:** November 24, 2026
**Re:** Kunoux Creamery, Inc.: review of the Tilil Systems DairyLedger license arrangement, issues and recommended fixes

---

## 1. Summary

You asked me to review the ten documents in the Kunoux / Tilil folder and set out Kunoux's position under the DairyLedger license arrangement. The documents are:

- the SaaS License Agreement;
- SOW No. 1;
- Amendment No. 1;
- Order Form No. 1;
- the January 2026 Term Sheet;
- the Parent Guaranty;
- the DPA;
- the Quality Agreement;
- the March 2026 press release; and
- the implementation kickoff minutes.

**Key commercial terms**

- **Parties.** Kunoux Creamery, Inc. is the Licensee. Tilil Systems, Inc. is the Licensor.
- **Term.** The License Agreement took effect on March 1, 2026. It has a **five-year Initial Term** under Section 14.1, followed by automatic one-year renewals under Section 14.2.
- **Fees.** The Annual Subscription Fee is $486,000 (Order Form §2.1), or $2,430,000 over the Initial Term.
- **Governing law.** Delaware (§16.1).
- **Guarantor.** **Kunoux Holdings, L.P.** is the guarantor under the Parent Guaranty. Under Parent Guaranty §§1.1 and 2.1 and Amendment No. 1 §6.2, it guarantees all of Kunoux's obligations under the Agreement as amended, as primary obligor.

**Issues in priority order**

| Priority | Issue | Location | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 (High: time-critical)** | The pending Ostrander sale triggers Tilil's change-of-control termination and fee-acceleration right | License Agreement §14.4 and §1 ("Change of Control"); Amendment No. 1, Recital B and §5.1 | Must be resolved before the expected Q1 2027 closing |
| **2 (High)** | Exclusivity reaches every current and future Kunoux and affiliate facility worldwide, not just the two Wisconsin plants | License Agreement §2.6; Order Form §3.1; contradicts Term Sheet §4.1 | Affects the Ostrander deal and any future M&A |
| **3 (Medium-High)** | Tilil can assign the agreement freely, including to a Kunoux competitor | License Agreement §15.1; §1 ("Permitted Transferee") | Raise in the same amendment |
| 4 (Lower) | Related clean-up points | Various | Include in the amendment package |

The documents in the folder do not resolve Issues 1–3. The press release and the kickoff minutes are background only. Both describe the deal as covering the two Wisconsin plants. That description supports our position on Issue 2, but it does not change the contract text.

I recommend that we approach Tilil now with a single Amendment No. 2 package. Its lead item should be change-of-control consent, because that is the point Tilil has leverage on and the one where timing matters.

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Ostrander acquisition triggers termination and fee acceleration (HIGH, time-critical)

**Where**

- License Agreement §14.4 (Change of Control).
- License Agreement §1 (definition of "Change of Control").
- Amendment No. 1, Recital B and §5.1.
- Parent Guaranty §1.1(b).

**What the documents say**

- **The trigger.** Section 14.4 lets Tilil terminate on **30 days' written notice** if Licensee "undergoes a Change of Control without Licensor's prior written consent."
- **The consequence.** On such a termination, "all Subscription Fees for the remainder of the Initial Term shall become immediately due and payable."
- **The definition.** Section 1 defines Change of Control to include "any direct or indirect transfer… of more than 50% of the voting equity of Licensee **or of any entity controlling Licensee**."
- **The pending sale.** Amendment No. 1, Recital B, records that on September 18, 2026 Kunoux Holdings, L.P. signed an equity purchase agreement. Under it, the equity of its general partner and operating subsidiaries will be sold to **Ostrander Dairy Partners III, L.P.**, with closing expected in Q1 2027.
- **No consent was given.** Amendment §5.1 states that, except as expressly set out in Sections 2 and 3, "**nothing herein constitutes a consent or waiver under the Agreement**." Sections 2 and 3 deal only with confidentiality, peak-season support, the status page, reporting, notices and SOW scheduling. None of them addresses change of control.
- **What follows.** Recording the deal in the Amendment does **not** amount to Tilil's consent. Nothing in the folder shows that consent has been requested or given.

**Why it matters to Kunoux**

- **Kunoux will be in a Change of Control.** The sale of Holdings' general partner and of the operating subsidiaries, which presumably include Kunoux itself, is at minimum an indirect transfer of more than 50% of the voting equity of an entity controlling Licensee.
- **Exposure is close to $2 million.** If closing occurs in Q1 2027, Tilil could terminate and demand the remaining Subscription Fees at once. If Year 1 has been paid, Years 2–5 total roughly **$1,944,000**. The Year 2 invoice date of March 1, 2027 falls in the same window.
- **Kunoux loses the platform and the fees.** Acceleration comes on top of losing access to the platform. Transition assistance under §14.6 is available, but Kunoux would pay for it.
- **The parent is also liable.** Parent Guaranty §1.1(b) expressly includes "amounts that become due and payable under Section 14.4" among the Guaranteed Obligations. Tilil could therefore pursue Kunoux Holdings directly, without first pursuing Kunoux (Guaranty §2.3).
- **The parent's liability survives the sale.** Guaranty §3.1(f) provides that a change in ownership does not discharge the Guaranty.
- **The buyer will care.** This liability will be relevant to the Ostrander purchase agreement. It is likely a disclosure item, and possibly a closing condition or indemnity item.
- **Tilil gains leverage.** Even if Tilil does not intend to terminate, the right gives it leverage to reprice or to resist our fixes on Issues 2 and 3.
- **Implementation timing.** The Sheboygan Go-Live (M6, January 18, 2027) and final acceptance (M7, February 17, 2027) fall in the same window as closing.
- **Notice obligation.** Kunoux must also notify Tilil within **10 Business Days after completion** of any Change of Control (§14.4, last sentence). Missing that notice would be a separate breach.

**Recommended fix**

1. **Seek Tilil's prior written consent now, well before closing.** The consent should cover the Ostrander transaction specifically. It should also confirm that the transaction will not give rise to any termination or acceleration right under §14.4. It must be signed by Tilil in accordance with §16.11.
2. **Narrow §14.4 for the future,** ideally in the same instrument:
   - exclude transfers to financial sponsors and other non-competitors;
   - require consent "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed"; and
   - replace full acceleration with, at most, a termination right without acceleration. An alternative is a cap tied to a short period of fees, for example 3–6 months.
3. **Coordinate with Holdings' M&A counsel.** The consent should be listed as a third-party consent in the equity purchase agreement, and its status should be tracked as a pre-closing deliverable.
4. **Calendar the post-closing notice.** The 10-Business-Day notice under §14.4 should be on the closing checklist as a backstop.

---

### Issue 2: Exclusivity covers every Kunoux and affiliate facility worldwide (HIGH)

**Where**

- License Agreement §2.6 (Exclusive Use), read with §1 ("Covered Facilities").
- Order Form §3.1.
- These contradict Term Sheet §4.1 and Annex A.

**What the documents say**

- **The covenant.** Section 2.6 provides that Licensee "shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, license, subscribe to or use any third-party software… that performs any of the Traceability Functions **at any Covered Facility**." It also bars internally developed tools used for those functions.
- **The License Agreement definition.** Section 1 defines Covered Facilities only by reference to the Order Form.
- **The Order Form definition.** Order Form §3.1 then defines Covered Facilities as "**all facilities owned, leased or operated by Licensee or any of its Affiliates, wherever located**." The definition covers processing plants, receiving stations, cold storage, distribution centers and laboratories. It also covers facilities acquired, leased or first operated *after* the Order Form date.
- **The Term Sheet deal.** Term Sheet §4.1 records the agreed position. Exclusivity was to "cover milk traceability software at the **Eau Claire and Sheboygan, Wisconsin plants only**." Term Sheet §3.5 adds that other facilities are "not part of this transaction."

**Why it matters to Kunoux**

- **Each provision looks harmless on its own.** Section 2.6 reads as a narrow covenant, and §3.1 reads as a generous license grant.
- **Together they reach the whole group, worldwide and into the future.** Read together, they impose exclusivity across every current and future facility of Kunoux and all its Affiliates.
- **Precedence does not help.** The §16.4 order-of-precedence clause does not rescue Kunoux, because there is no conflict between the documents. Section 2.6 simply incorporates the Order Form definition.
- **The Term Sheet does not help either.** It is non-binding (Term Sheet §14.1), and its pricing hold expired on March 31, 2026.
- **The Ostrander effect.** After closing, Ostrander's other portfolio companies may become "Affiliates" of Kunoux under the 50%-control test in §1. Kunoux would then be obliged to "cause its Affiliates not to" use competing traceability tools at *their* facilities. Ostrander is unlikely to accept that, and it could become a closing issue or a breach risk.
- **Future acquisitions are caught.** Any plant Kunoux later acquires would have to migrate to DairyLedger or be in breach. There is no carve-out for existing contracts at acquired sites.
- **Tilil has no matching obligation.** The SOW (§2.8(a)) and Order Form (§3.3) put implementation at any other facility outside scope. Kunoux could therefore be barred from using alternatives at a site where Tilil has not deployed and need not deploy without a further paid SOW.

**Recommended fix**

1. **Amend §2.6 to match the Term Sheet.** Limit the covenant expressly to the **Eau Claire Plant and the Sheboygan Plant**, for example by replacing "at any Covered Facility" with "at the Eau Claire Plant or the Sheboygan Plant (as defined in the SOW)."
2. **Fallback position.** Add a separate, narrower "Exclusive Facilities" definition for §2.6 purposes, while leaving the broader Covered Facilities definition for license-grant purposes. It may suit Kunoux to keep the right to *use* DairyLedger anywhere.
3. **Carve-outs to add in either case:**
   - facilities of Affiliates that are not Kunoux's subsidiaries, including any sponsor portfolio companies;
   - facilities acquired after the Order Form date, with at least a grace period and protection for existing third-party contracts; and
   - facilities at which Tilil has not completed implementation.
4. **Use the background documents in negotiation.** Rely on the Term Sheet, the press release (which announces deployment "at its processing plants in Eau Claire and Sheboygan") and the kickoff minutes as evidence of the commercial deal. They do not, however, have contractual effect.

---

### Issue 3: Tilil can assign freely, including to a Kunoux competitor (MEDIUM-HIGH)

**Where**

- License Agreement §15.1 (Assignment).
- License Agreement §1 (definition of "Permitted Transferee").
- Related: Parent Guaranty §7.1.

**What the documents say**

- **Section 15.1 appears mutual.** Neither party may assign without the other's consent, "except that either party may assign this Agreement in its entirety to a **Permitted Transferee** upon written notice."
- **The definition is not mutual.** Permitted Transferee means:
  - (a) any Affiliate of either party; or
  - (b) "any successor to all or **any part of Licensor's business** or assets to which this Agreement relates."
- **Limb (b) is one-sided.** It applies only to Tilil and has no counterpart for Kunoux.

**Why it matters to Kunoux**

- **Tilil can assign without consent.** Tilil can assign the Agreement on mere notice to any buyer of *any part* of its business, for example a buyer of only the DairyLedger product line.
- **No protective conditions apply.** There is no requirement that the buyer be creditworthy, assume the Agreement in writing, or not be a competitor.
- **The buyer could be a rival.** It could be a rival dairy processor or cooperative, or its technology arm.
- **Highly sensitive data would follow the contract.** Kunoux's Licensee Data includes farm supplier identities, pickup volumes, pricing and premium data, quality results and organic certification records (§1 "Licensee Data"; DPA Schedule 1). The §8.2 restrictions on benchmarking would bind an assignee, but in practice Kunoux would be relying on a competitor's compliance.
- **Exclusivity and the guaranty would follow too.** Kunoux would remain locked into exclusivity under §2.6 (see Issue 2) in favor of that new counterparty. Under Parent Guaranty §7.1, the benefit of the guaranty would also pass automatically to the assignee.
- **The arrangement is asymmetric.** Kunoux needs consent for any transfer outside its Affiliates.

**Recommended fix**

1. **Narrow limb (b) of the definition** to a successor to **all or substantially all** of Tilil's business or assets to which the Agreement relates, provided that the successor:
   - (i) is **not a Kunoux competitor**, a term to be defined to cover dairy processors and cooperatives and their affiliates;
   - (ii) assumes the Agreement in writing; and
   - (iii) has financial and technical capability at least equal to Tilil's.
2. **Require advance notice.** Tilil should give at least 30 days' prior written notice of any assignment.
3. **Give Kunoux a termination right if the transferee is a competitor.** The right should be exercisable without penalty, with a refund of prepaid fees, transition assistance under §14.6 at no extra charge, and release from §2.6.
4. **Make the change mutual, or add a Kunoux equivalent.** Kunoux should be able to assign to a successor to all or substantially all of its business, which also helps on Issue 1.
5. **Conform Parent Guaranty §7.1** so that the guaranty passes only on an assignment permitted under the revised §15.1.

---

### Issue 4: Lower-priority clean-up points (LOWER)

These are not urgent, but they should go into the same amendment package.

- **Confidentiality: disclosure to prospective acquirers (Amendment No. 1 §2.1).** Amended §10.3(b) now allows each party to disclose Confidential Information to prospective acquirers and their advisers. This helps Kunoux share the Agreement with Ostrander. It equally allows Tilil to share Kunoux information with prospective buyers of Tilil, who could include competitors (see Issue 3). Personal data and some security materials are carved out, but supplier pricing and volume data held as Licensee Data are not expressly excluded from Tilil-side disclosure.
  *Fix:* exclude Licensee Data from clause (ii) disclosures by Licensor, or limit those disclosures to non-competitors.
- **Breadth of the Guaranty (Parent Guaranty §§1.1, 1.2 and 3.1(a)).**
  - The Term Sheet (§1.2(f)) contemplated a guaranty of Kunoux's *payment* obligations.
  - The executed Guaranty covers all payment *and performance* obligations.
  - It applies to future amendments "whether or not the Guarantor has consented," including amendments that add facilities or fees.
  *Fix:* when Holdings acknowledges Amendment No. 2, confirm the guaranty's scope. Consider asking for release or substitution of the guarantor after the Ostrander closing, since Holdings' ownership position will change.
